target: Feature parity is the requested target. No smaller V1 scope has been approved.

sources.note: Grouped capability inventory, including plan-labelled additions; not all are free or included in StarterKit.
Node, mark, command, shortcut and decoration extensibility.
Table commands, selections and optional resizing.
Image presentation and optional inline/resize behavior; upload is a separate integration.
Yjs and IndexedDB offline integration; not Breditor's protocol.
Inspected optional extension assembly; includes Underline, Link and structural helpers.
Inspected command surface, table plugin wiring and separate HTML/Markdown converters.
Modern comparison target for the FCKeditor lineage; configurable UI and integrations.
More than 150 features/subfeatures, with premium labels. Rows below group related capabilities rather than copy that count.
Rich table workflow, including capabilities beyond basic geometry.
External document paste is a dedicated feature, not internal clipboard equivalence.
Inspected separate input transformation, model insertion and output transformation stages. No source copied.
Open-source and commercial feature boundaries must be evaluated separately.
Legacy CKEditor 4 reached ordinary EOL in June 2023; not the modern baseline.

features.summary: Paragraph and heading editing
features.current: Rust rich actions and the shared editor support paragraphs, ranked headings, split/join and retained identity.
features.acceptance: Keep all six heading ranks, text formatting, local/shared history and recovery consistent in one installed V1 editor.

features.summary: Bold, italic, underline, strike and inline code
features.current: Default Showcase supports several marks. The rich/shared default toolbar exposes Bold; its render hook admits only span/strong/em/code. Underline is not a shipped integrated control.
features.acceptance: Ship all everyday marks in the combined profile, renderer and toolbar; test mixed state, caret formats, clipboard, offline edits and selective Undo/Redo.

features.summary: Subscript and superscript
features.current: Typed formats provide a foundation, not integrated subscript/superscript behavior or controls.
features.acceptance: Define mutually compatible script formats, semantic presentation and exact history/interchange behavior.

features.summary: Font family, size, text and background color
features.current: Default Showcase has bounded RGB24 text color, discrete text sizes and Highlight. Those policies are not integrated into the shared renderer; general font families/background colors are not complete.
features.acceptance: Promote safe declarative presentations into the combined editor, define supported font/size/color domains and test interoperability.

features.summary: Links and automatic link detection
features.current: Safe Link forms and typed values work in the default profile. The combined renderer has no anchor recipe; autolink is not an integrated feature.
features.acceptance: Use one safe URL policy for shared rendering, explicit link editing, clipboard/export and optional autolink, without interpreting arbitrary HTML.

features.summary: Blockquotes, code blocks and horizontal rules
features.current: The admitted rich flow grammar contains paragraph, heading, lists, table and image, not these three common block kinds.
features.acceptance: Add original Rust contracts and separate actions for each kind, including code language/text rules, boundary navigation, shared conflict policy and migration.

features.summary: Hard breaks and navigation around atomic blocks
features.current: The shared input bridge inserts LF for insertLineBreak and supports node/grid navigation. That is not a separately specified hard-break node or a complete gap/drop/trailing-block experience.
features.acceptance: Specify soft-break semantics, create reachable text positions around every atom, and test Shift+Enter, arrows, deletion and empty-document recovery.

features.summary: Bullet and numbered nested lists
features.current: Rich and shared paths implement indentation, outdentation, item split/join and list conversion with retained content.
features.acceptance: Retain the same list contract in the V1 installable profile and native/browser mixed-content tests.

features.summary: Interactive task lists
features.current: The sealed rich grammar has no task item or checked-state contract.
features.acceptance: Add typed checked state with keyboard and pointer behavior, nesting, clipboard, conflict policy and author-local history.

features.summary: List numbering and marker properties
features.current: Positive ordered-list starts are supported. Reversed numbering, marker families and legal multilevel counters are not an integrated feature set.
features.acceptance: Define each numbering/style domain, restart/continuation behavior and deterministic nested export before claiming advanced list parity.

features.summary: Alignment, block indent, direction and line height controls
features.current: The current combined toolbar has list indentation but no complete block layout property family.
features.acceptance: Add bounded semantic block properties, direction-aware selection/layout and safe rendering/interchange, not arbitrary stored CSS.

features.summary: Text, node, grid and document-wide editing selections
features.current: Stable text/node/grid selections exist. Rich range replacement covers one block, sibling flow and sibling list heads, not arbitrary cross-container ranges.
features.acceptance: Specify and implement document-wide Select All, deletion, replacement and formatting across lists, tables, captions and atoms in both directions.

features.summary: Undo, Redo and natural typing groups
features.current: Exact local and selective shared history/reload are implemented. Natural typing coalescing and the final integrated boundary policy are not qualified.
features.acceptance: Define typing/paste/composition/format/move grouping, preserve remote work under local Undo, and test future Redo after recovery.

features.summary: Breditor structural clipboard
features.current: Original rich JSON and plain text support copied text, flow and table grids with fresh identities. This is not Office or generic HTML paste.
features.acceptance: Keep exact source preservation, one-step cut/paste history and cross-peer clipboard behavior in the installed V1 editor.

features.summary: Sanitized HTML import and semantic export
features.current: Default clipboard emits checked HTML and flattens an admitted HTML subset to plain text. Combined paste consumes original rich JSON/plain text, not general rich HTML.
features.acceptance: Build separate import/export adapters with declared loss diagnostics, resource bounds, URL policy, asset references and rich round-trip fixtures.

features.summary: Markdown import, export and paste
features.current: There is no combined Markdown data adapter; canonical Breditor JSON remains distinct.
features.acceptance: Choose a versioned Markdown subset, preserve representable semantics, report losses for merges/styles/media and test round trips.

features.summary: Word, Google Docs and spreadsheet rich paste
features.current: Internal fragments and plain text do not preserve foreign formatting, list structure or spreadsheet tables.
features.acceptance: Maintain real producer fixtures and sanitization/loss policies; test lists, styles, tables, links and images through the same Rust admission boundary.

features.summary: Table geometry, cell bodies and grid operations
features.current: Creation/removal, row/column edits/moves, headers, merge/split, width values, rich cells and grid navigation/clipboard are functionally tested.
features.acceptance: Preserve the complete command set, rich content and selective history under the production package and all supported engines.

features.summary: Table presentation and advanced interaction
features.current: Width/header controls exist. Drag resize, table captions and style/property panels are incomplete. Nested tables are intentionally outside the current admitted rich grammar.
features.acceptance: Resolve nested-table policy explicitly; add captions, accessible resize handles, table/cell presentation and interoperable rich paste without losing source partitions.

features.summary: Block raster images and durable assets
features.current: PNG/JPEG/WebP file admission, paste/drop, alt/decorative, captions, dimensions, replacement/removal, offline uploads and cross-host bytes are implemented.
features.acceptance: Preserve byte-first durability, binding epochs, cancelled uploads and independent document/asset save indicators in the V1 package.

features.summary: Image layouts, handles, links and external sources
features.current: Numeric dimensions and block captions work. Inline/wrapped images, drag handles, image links, responsive variants and safe remote-URL ingestion are not a complete product workflow.
features.acceptance: Define supported layouts and ingestion policy, then test resize gestures, responsive output, link/alt behavior and asset lifecycle. Do not turn remote URLs into implicit server fetches.

features.summary: Simultaneous rich editing and selective history
features.current: Rust replicas and the reference relay integrate concurrent text, list, table and image edits while retaining author-local Undo/Redo.
features.acceptance: Keep the native contracts and independent-browser mixed workflow passing against the final released artifacts.

features.summary: Offline editing, reconnect and exact reload
features.current: Exclusive writer ownership, durable local journals, queued uploads, reconnect and restart recovery work through real browser/network tests.
features.acceptance: Qualify supported history/document limits and operational recovery, not only the normal offline/reconnect path.

features.summary: Authenticated peer carets and selections
features.current: Lease-bound ephemeral presence resolves causal text/node/grid anchors and paints a separate read-only overlay.
features.acceptance: Retain expiry, fencing and read-only behavior; qualify overlay placement and accessibility in the supported layouts.

features.summary: Permissions and application authentication
features.current: Reference-room Reader/Editor authority and revocation are enforced. The local demo bootstrap is not public login, tenant provisioning or TLS deployment.
features.acceptance: Provide host identity adapters, room lifecycle, secure credential storage, observable denial/revocation and deployment guidance with independent authorization tests.

features.summary: Read-only and restricted editing UI
features.current: A relay Reader role is not a read-only DOM editor contract. SharedDomOptions has no complete read-only/restricted-editing mode.
features.acceptance: Enforce read-only consistently for keyboard, beforeinput, clipboard, API, toolbar, composition and remote updates; define editable-region restrictions separately.

features.summary: Composable feature and custom-node SDK
features.current: Typed inline declarations, profile fingerprints and custom toolbar callbacks exist. Shared structural grammar is sealed; arbitrary custom blocks/node views are not a supported extension SDK.
features.acceptance: Stabilize Breditor-owned schema/action/render/converter capabilities, dependencies, failure isolation and conformance tests without adopting another editor's protocol.

features.summary: Expandable toolbars, context menus and selection UI
features.current: Both paths have extensible toolbars, but the shared path does not reuse the default compiled action-state/form system or provide a complete contextual/floating menu experience.
features.acceptance: One command/state contract must drive buttons, keyboard, forms and context menus with active/mixed/disabled state and consistent focus return.

features.summary: Find and replace
features.current: There is no integrated document search/decorations/replacement workflow.
features.acceptance: Define literal/Unicode search, navigation and replace-all as one bounded semantic action, excluding hidden or noneditable content by explicit policy.

features.summary: Markdown shortcuts and automatic text transformations
features.current: Explicit semantic commands are implemented; typed pattern recognition and reversible input rules are not an integrated feature.
features.acceptance: Add deterministic opt-in rules with composition exclusion, remote-edit boundaries and one-step Undo behavior.

features.summary: Mentions and slash commands
features.current: There is no supported suggestion session or durable mention entity contract.
features.acceptance: Specify entity identity, async suggestion cancellation, accessible menus and command execution through Rust rather than DOM mutation.

features.summary: Counts, placeholder, fullscreen and outline
features.current: No unified public utility package supplies these workflows for the combined editor.
features.acceptance: Derive counts/outline from admitted AST snapshots, keep placeholders out of content, and preserve focus/selection through fullscreen transitions.

features.summary: Block rearrangement and drop feedback
features.current: File drop and typed block/axis moves exist; a general block drag handle, semantic drop target and drop cursor UI are incomplete.
features.acceptance: Move retained IDs rather than copy/delete; add keyboard equivalents and test invalid/cyclic/cross-container targets and shared Undo.

features.summary: Media, details, emoji, math and diagrams
features.current: Unicode text is supported, but that is not a typed emoji picker, equation, collapsible section, audio/video or diagram widget.
features.acceptance: Use separate original node contracts, inert/sandboxed renderers and explicit providers. Define import/export and collaboration for each admitted widget.

features.summary: Framework integrations and static rendering
features.current: A framework-neutral runtime and default React reference exist. A production rich/shared React integration, SSR/static renderer and broader framework examples are not complete.
features.acceptance: Ship installed-package React and vanilla examples, stable lifecycle hooks and an inert data renderer; document adapter responsibility for other frameworks.

features.summary: Threaded comments and review annotations
features.current: Internal format/provenance annotations and presence anchors are not a comment product: no durable discussion, resolution or review sidebar API exists.
features.acceptance: Design durable mapped anchors, thread permissions, resolution/orphan policy, offline merging and independent comment history before building UI.

features.summary: Suggestions and tracked changes
features.current: Operation provenance/selective Undo is not accept/reject review mode.
features.acceptance: Define suggestions for text, formatting, lists, tables and images with attribution, permissions, concurrent accept/reject and explicit export semantics.

features.summary: Named versions, comparison and restore
features.current: Exact journals and recovery exist; there is no named revision browser, semantic diff or shared restore-as-new-change workflow.
features.acceptance: Separate user-facing document versions from runtime journals and GC; restore without reusing old writer identity or overwriting concurrent work.

features.summary: Word, PDF and other office document conversion
features.current: Breditor JSON backup/export is not DOCX/PDF/ODT conversion or layout fidelity.
features.acceptance: Choose self-hostable adapters, licensing and fidelity targets; preserve document/asset bindings and report unsupported content instead of silently dropping it.

features.summary: Pages, page breaks and print layout
features.current: The editor is a continuous flow surface, not a paginated document layout engine.
features.acceptance: Keep page layout separate from canonical rich flow where possible; define deterministic print/export expectations for tables, captions and images.

features.summary: Templates, merge fields, footnotes and bookmarks
features.current: Stable internal block IDs are not user bookmarks, references, template fields or footnotes.
features.acceptance: Design reference integrity, field/value trust, permissions and shared history; define behavior when referenced content is moved or removed.

features.summary: AI assistance and integrated spelling or grammar review
features.current: Browser-native spelling behavior is not a provider, review UI or semantic AI command integration.
features.acceptance: Define explicit host providers and privacy boundaries; generated edits must use ordinary guarded commands with stale-result rejection and reviewable history.

features.summary: Source editing, general HTML and email layouts
features.current: Canonical schema-bound AST editing deliberately does not preserve arbitrary HTML/CSS, full-page metadata or email layout markup.
features.acceptance: Resolve the compatibility scope explicitly. Any source UI must import through a bounded allowlist and loss report; never store executable HTML as trusted editor state.

features.summary: Multiple editable roots in one document
features.current: Multiple independent editor instances exist, but they do not establish a shared multi-root document selection/history contract.
features.acceptance: Specify root identity, cross-root selections, shared ordering and one history owner before advertising multi-root parity.

features.summary: Localized UI, bidirectional content and language metadata
features.current: Unicode text is retained, but shared controls are English and RTL/bidirectional editing, localized commands and text-part language are not qualified as a supported product surface.
features.acceptance: Separate UI language from content direction, localize control strings and qualify mixed-direction navigation/selection with language metadata.

gates.acceptance: Expand grouped rows into versioned acceptance cases for every selected Tiptap/CKEditor capability. Group counts are not a parity percentage; record intentional differences and obtain approval for exclusions.

gates.summary: Promote rich/shared Rust, Wasm and browser packages
gates.acceptance: Independent clean consumers install one supported paired profile and production module; no experiments path, manual target artifact or source-only link is required.

gates.summary: Freeze V1 APIs and explicit migration contracts
gates.acceptance: Document source, ABI, schema, journal and asset compatibility separately; add supported old-version recovery/migration fixtures and deliberate rejection paths.

gates.summary: Cover every distributed feature in the release pipeline
gates.acceptance: Default verify:release alone is insufficient. Run default, rich, shared, relay and installed-consumer checks reproducibly in CI, retaining exact candidate hashes and failed runs.

gates.summary: Qualify browser faults and native clipboard
gates.acceptance: Close or explicitly resolve the historical WebKit fault with a reproducible cause/fix or supported-environment policy, and qualify native Safari/Chrome plus repeated lifecycle/clipboard sessions. Passing isolated files is not an engine repair.

gates.summary: Qualify physical input, accessibility and touch
gates.acceptance: On the final integrated artifact, complete real IME, screen-reader, keyboard-only and supported mobile/touch testing. Earlier bounded or synthetic cases do not certify V1.

gates.summary: Approve measured latency, memory and download budgets
gates.acceptance: Set supported document/table/image/history/peer sizes and measure startup, typing, paste, Undo, reconnect and long-session memory on named hardware/browser versions. Do not silently raise existing default budgets.

Provide import/decode work isolation, TLS/identity/tenant integration, abuse limits, observability and deployment tests. Loopback demo tokens and best-effort decoder limits are not public production isolation.

gates.summary: Handle history limits, backup and compaction
gates.acceptance: Define document lifetime at current journal/log/asset bounds, safe compaction and asset retention, restore drills and credential/writer recovery without cloning a live author.

gates.summary: Audit the actual V1 dependency and license graph
gates.acceptance: Generate and review notices/SBOM for browser, Wasm and native relay artifacts, including the pinned replication patch and decoders; verify reproducibility and vulnerability response ownership.

gates.summary: Ship coherent SDK documentation and support policy
gates.acceptance: Publish one install/quickstart, capability/support matrix, host asset/auth responsibilities, security reporting, troubleshooting, upgrade guide and contribution policy that match the actual archives.
Run sustained mixed-content use with independent collaborators, disconnects, reloads and backup restoration; record incidents, data integrity and supported operating limits.
After all required scope and qualification work, tag a reviewed RC, verify clean installs and every gate against immutable hashes, then obtain separate publication/deployment approval.
